title: Nos Vemos en las Urnas: a useful private quiz for the 2023 Congress election
subtitle: Real programmes, directly authored questions, verified meaning and a modern readable quiz
summary: Build a quiz for ordinary Spanish users based explicitly on the 23 July 2023 Congress election. Acquire the complete official candidacy corpus, read available programmes in full one by one, cross-reference policies and directly author a larger balanced question bank. Correct and prove the full answer/citation/scoring path, then replace the basic UI with an accessible smooth quiz. Defer programme-comparison screens, metrics expansion and optional languages. This is a new acceptance baseline, not a claim that the existing synthetic implementation satisfies the request.
baseline: 30 new Q001-Q030 increments with explicit acceptance; L001-L030 are retained historical progress only
Confirmed scope: every applicable candidacy in all 52 Congress constituencies for 23 July 2023
Real public edition; synthetic fixtures remain internal tests only
Source download and semantic analysis are separate statuses; 3 files downloaded, 0 complete readings, 0 released real questions at this planning baseline
One PHP app, fixed public bank, private browser-memory answers; no runtime model or new infrastructure

sections.title: 1. Confirmed 2023 quiz scope
sections.lead: One useful private quiz for ordinary users; all real Congress candidacies.
items: The owner confirmed the 23 July 2023 general election and Congress. Label every intro/result/export as the 2023 edition, never as current political evidence.
Q001-Q030 supersede the previous L sequence for this iteration. Preserve the earlier engineering evidence, but do not reuse completed labels as proof of real-source correctness.
Programme-comparison screens, aggregate-feedback expansion and optional languages are deferred. Keep a compact source/evidence disclosure that supports the quiz.
No new accounts, backoffice, reviewer/quorum programme, runtime AI, scheduler, repository restart or history rewrite.

sections.title: 2. Everyday-user quiz journey
sections.lead: Understand a practical question, answer comfortably and receive an explanation.
items: One concrete decision per question; one affirmative grammatical proposition whose positive answer always means agreeing with that exact proposition.
Spanish statement normally 12-25 words; if a longer statement is necessary preserve meaning and explain why. No unexplained acronym, double negation, two policies or leading moral label.
Optional neutral explanation, normally 25-45 words, describes what the proposal means; use everyday money/work/home/school/health/transport examples only when they preserve actual conditions.
Explain essential terms at first use (for example, the income tax on earnings); do not silently broaden a targeted tax into all taxes or a regional rule into all of Spain.
No unsupported impact forecast, guaranteed cheaper rent, inflation estimate or assertion that an opinion is correct. Plain-language examples are not proof of policy effects.
No party names, logos or ideological answer labels while answering. Original-language quotations and party identity become available in result evidence after deliberate finish.
No technical methodology/hashes/uncertainty tables in the main journey; retain source and method details behind clearly named optional disclosures.
Start with a short Spanish explanation of the observed proposal overlap, not a voting instruction or a personality/ideology classification.

Show three understandable cited agreements and three disagreements when available, each with Your answer / What the programme proposes / How they relate. Do not fabricate six examples when evidence is absent.
Distinguish a disagreement on one proposal from total overlap across other proposals. A top overall result may disagree with the user on rent caps; label that disagreement explicitly.
Explain missing evidence as We could not find a clear position in this programme, never Neutral or They oppose it.
For fair ordering, explain These candidacies were compared using the same N questions; show other eligible candidacies and coverage. For insufficient evidence do not announce a winner.
Use a percentage only as a secondary explained policy-overlap index; no probability, confidence, sum-to-100 rule or definitive You are aligned with this party.
Start with one clear CTA; choosing a province determines eligible parties locally. Topic priorities are optional later settings, not an entry form the average user must configure.
Ten questions offer a short start; optional blocks of five allow a deeper 15/20/25/30-question session. More questions must add distinct useful evidence, not repetition.

sections.title: 3. Complete real programme corpus
sections.lead: Establish the denominator before claiming all programmes.
items: Use the BOE proclaimed candidacies, corrections and final results to reconcile all 52 constituencies. Initial results inventory has 59 official denominations, not yet 59 verified programme owners.

Search every inventory row, including minor/no-seat/territorial candidacies. Prefer original dated party/coalition publications; use verified preserved originals when links are broken and label the source chain.

Download byte-checked bounded original PDFs/HTML locally; retain requested/resolved URL, publication/election evidence, retrieval date, original SHA-256, extraction SHA-256, language, owner and explicit territorial applicability.

Keep original PDFs/HTML/extractions in the ignored local cache; track reproducible provenance, acquisition failures, authored notes and small permitted public excerpts. Public access does not itself assign an open-source licence to a programme.

Separate not searched, located, retrieval failed, downloaded, extracted, fully read, mapped and validated. Record dated attempts and missing/unpublished/unavailable documents explicitly; never fabricate a programme or borrow another election.

An unavailable programme does not remove the candidacy. A coalition member programme is not inherited without documented applicable adoption; do not count component parties as separate ballot choices.

sections.title: 4. Read first, cross-reference, then author
sections.lead: The agent directly reads every available full programme and writes the bank; no automatic question generator.
items: For each document, read all sections/page ranges, including annexes and footnotes; write an individual issue notebook with exact quotes, PDF and printed page, conditions, scope, rationale and unknowns. A download, extraction or keyword hit is not a completed reading.

Cross-reference individual notebooks into an issue matrix before finalising question wording. For every candidature/question pair explicitly record support, opposition, qualified position, unknown or conflict with source references.

Author a target bank of 80 distinct everyday Spanish questions; release at least 60 supported questions across at least ten topics. No padding, duplicate policies, silent unsupported values or paraphrased source quotes.

State an explicit question-specific scale rubric: +2 means clear agreement with the exact shown proposition, -2 clear opposition; +/-1 only with a justified qualified stance; 0 only explicitly evidenced intermediate/neutral position, never silence or a conflict.

Every scored mapping retains contextual quotation, party/programme identity, page/range, rationale and rubric. Preserve negation, quantities, exceptions and territorial applicability. Treat whole-law repeal versus one provision carefully; do not infer a stance on every clause from a broad slogan.

Automate extraction, hashing, schema/quote validation and selection among already authored question IDs only. No scheduled/model/keyword generator may create questions, help texts or numeric positions for the release. Existing literal fixtures are engineering tests only.

sections.title: 5. Verify meaning and arithmetic together
sections.lead: Trace the full result instead of guessing a global sign correction.
items: Canonical labels run -2 Strongly disagree through +2 Strongly agree in an explicit ordered array. Verify browser-visible order, chosen value, stored state, authored direction, source value and result explanation.
Retain deterministic similarity 1-abs(answer-position)/4 unless a documented defect justifies a versioned change. Independent expected cases: -2 versus +2 = 0; -2 versus -2 = 1; 0 versus +/-2 = 0.5.

Build an independent semantic calibration ledger for every released question and mapping, with source-grounded expected support/opposition and calculation cases. Do not calculate expected answers by calling the same implementation under test.

Test all five user answers, inverse phrasing, qualifications, missing/conflicting data, skip/unsure, edited answers, ties, duplicates and weighting. Rent-cap strongly disagree versus a supporting party must be marked a disagreement even if that party has the highest aggregate overlap.

Use fixed topic/family budgets and an eligible constituency cohort determined independently of answers. Rank only parties sharing identical scored propositions and weights above the declared minimums; disclose the fixed comparison subset and preserve other eligible candidacies.
Never convert silence to neutral, compare differently covered partial scores in one leaderboard, silently discard small parties, label overlap a probability or split 100 percent among parties.

sections.title: 6. Larger authored bank, comfortable sessions
sections.lead: Selection chooses existing questions; it does not generate content.
items: Initial ten questions balance distinct topics and policy families. Optional five-question blocks use unseen authored questions, improve coverage and cap redundancy.

Exercise actual constituency cohorts, including missing-programme candidacies, so a minor unknown party does not silently disappear or force a misleading full ranking. Insufficient fair evidence gets an honest unranked outcome.
Keep unsure/skip separate from the neutral numerical answer. Allow revisiting/editing; explain more answers may change results in either direction.
No race, countdown, correct-answer feedback or completion-forced result. Retain deliberate finish, frozen release per session, local reset and explicit local export.

sections.title: 7. A modern readable quiz stage
sections.lead: A concrete interaction design, not a skin on the old form.
items: Quiz stage inspired by the clear one-question interaction of Kahoot, with a calm credible civic identity. No trivia right/wrong, speed score, countdown, competitive leaderboard or party-coloured answer buttons.
Palette: ink #182235, canvas #F4F7FB, surface #FFFFFF, action #3449A4, muted #526078, selected #176B71

Reuse the existing locally served font assets after inspecting them; strong readable sans headings, body 18px on mobile, line height 1.5-1.65, bounded line lengths; no third-party font request or dependency changes.
Compact persistent edition/progress line; topic name; one large question; optional What does this mean? help.
Five equally prominent labelled agreement choices in a stable disagree-to-agree order; separate unsure and skip controls. Native radio group, no hover-only controls.
Back/edit and one primary Continue action remain clear; selection has an immediate visible state, but no automatic advancement.
Checkpoint after ten: See my result or Five more questions; always explicit finish. Result page has plain-language agreement/difference evidence and a quiet source disclosure.

Short 160-220ms opacity/transform transitions between questions and clear selected-state feedback; no layout jump, double submission or lost focus. prefers-reduced-motion removes movement and preserves feedback.

44px minimum touch targets, visible keyboard focus, radio keyboard semantics, text contrast at least 4.5:1, control/focus contrast at least 3:1; 320px reflow and 200/400% zoom; never encode direction only by colour. Verify the actual palette in each state.

Inspect actual desktop/mobile screenshots for intro/question/help/selected/checkpoint/results/loading/error states and perform keyboard/reduced-motion checks; no design task is complete from CSS or descriptions alone.

sections.title: 8. Preserve the private quiz boundary
sections.lead: A simpler interface must preserve local processing.
items: Fetch the same fixed public versioned bank for everyone. Province, answers, priorities, adaptive state, results and finished state stay only in browser memory by default.
No personalised API, party/result URL, answer telemetry, persistent identifier, raw request log or remote crash payload containing private state. Help content and scoring remain local.
Do not embed third-party video, analytics, fonts or programme viewers in the answering journey. Explicit original-source links after finish may open the external publisher with no referrer.
Finish is not collection consent. Preserve the optional feedback implementation disabled and defer its product work.

sections.title: 9. Deferred optional feedback
sections.lead: Accuracy and usefulness of the quiz come first.
items: Do not expand, enable or present optional feedback as a core quiz dependency. Preserve the bounded counters and separate consent design for a later iteration.
Any future activation still excludes raw quiz answers/party/scores/district/identifiers, requires actual hosted privacy/log/notice checks and remains part of explicit PUBLIC-LAUNCH approval.

sections.title: 10. Plain Spanish and inclusive interface
items: All public questions, explanations, buttons, errors, privacy/help and local export labels are Spanish. Original code/routes/keys/comments/tests/developer docs are English. Keep lang/es semantic keys and es default/fallback.

Audit every authored question for one concrete decision, unexplained jargon, leading framing and loss of source conditions. Short help explains meaning without advertising an answer or inventing impacts.
Original quotations/proper names remain exact. Translated source explanations are labelled paraphrases, with the original accessible after finish.
Optional ca/gl/eu remain deferred; enabled translations later preserve IDs/scales/citation meaning and scores, with incomplete packs disabled.

Native controls, keyboard/focus, contrast, reduced motion, mobile reflow and Spanish screen-reader names are required. Existing automated checks plus a practical reproducible walkthrough are sufficient; no recruited certification panel.

sections.title: 11. Reuse the lean app
sections.lead: Source work is local; quiz execution stays small.
items: Reuse Laravel/Blade/Tailwind v4/TypeScript, immutable public bundles, hashes, release withdrawal and local matching. No dependency change, additional runtime worker/model or database infrastructure is required by this plan.
Retain SQLite feedback counters disabled; no new paid analytics or hosting purchase. Keep original source cache excluded from Git and public assets.
Measure full real-bank size against existing public payload limits; compact excerpt-only citations without deleting context essential to the interpretation. No answer-dependent fetches.

sections.title: 12. Real-source and user-visible acceptance
sections.lead: Passing synthetic CI does not certify the 2023 edition.
items: Completion requires a reconciled full candidacy inventory; an acquisition/missing record for every row; full authored readings for every used programme; a crossed issue matrix; at least sixty useful validated questions; and audited mappings/citations.

A missing programme remains explicitly missing and unscored. All available programme texts must be analysed before calling corpus analysis complete; never claim every programme was downloaded if some are unavailable.
Independently checked rent and inverse cases, exact quotation/range/page checks and browser label-to-result regressions are release blockers. Fix defects before recording completion.

Verify actual mobile/desktop states, keyboard, reduced motion, no-party-reveal-before-finish, answer editing and network/storage privacy. Record the ordinary-user walkthrough and revise confusing copy.
Run existing required CI/security/dependency audits and the exact staged tree gate before every commit. Keep local test evidence distinct from hosted checks and production readiness.
Prepare a concrete 2023 release/host/cost/privacy/rollback packet before PUBLIC-LAUNCH; do not publish, activate collection or push automatically.

sections.title: 13. Future programmes are a separate edition
sections.lead: Replace evidence deliberately when new programmes arrive.
items: Preserve the 2023 edition with its sources, question meaning and corrections. New election metadata, candidacies, programmes and authored semantic readings produce a new release, not a date substitution.
Reuse a question only if its exact proposition/rubric remains applicable and every new scored position has new applicable citations; never inherit party values automatically.
Pin existing sessions to their original edition; correction/withdrawal and rollback use immutable hashes. Programme comparison, metrics expansion and optional translations remain later work.

sections.title: 14. How loop engineer proceeds
sections.lead: Work one inspectable increment at a time with factual evidence.
items: Read docs/loop-engineer.md, the canonical plan and outputs/quiz-2023-scope-revision.json. Keep the old implementation session paused; no scheduler or task message is started.

For source tasks select one pending inventory document, acquire/extract/read it fully and save its individual notes. Continue across documents and turns until every available programme has been read; do not mark the parent complete after one party.

After individual readings, cross-check each issue across programmes, author and calibrate questions, then implement the quiz design. Independent source retries and design preparation may proceed when a particular link is unavailable.
Record actual commands, original/source hashes, reading page ranges, authored artefacts, defect fixes and tests in work/execution-journal.jsonl. Status changes require the actual acceptance evidence.
Preserve working/index/history and use direct main commits only after all required staged checks. No new reset, history rewrite, branches, worktrees, identity changes or automatic push.

requirements.title: Useful quiz without prerequisites
requirements.acceptance: The main journey uses concrete everyday Spanish, one decision per question, short neutral help and understandable reasons; no analyst dashboard, account or paywall.

requirements.title: Complete 2023 coverage
requirements.acceptance: All 23J Congress candidacies are reconciled across 52 constituencies, with acquisition attempts, applicability, provenance and explicit missing records; no four-party shortcut.

requirements.title: Direct reading and authored evidence
requirements.acceptance: Every used programme is read in full by the agent; questions and numeric mappings are directly authored after cross-reference, with exact context and no automatic generator.

requirements.title: Quiz-first scope
requirements.acceptance: The home and primary journey are the quiz. Standalone programme-comparison screens and metrics expansion are deferred; keep only source disclosures needed to explain results.

requirements.title: Private deterministic matching
requirements.acceptance: Private answers/province/priorities/results remain in browser memory; same fixed public bank; no personalised API, telemetry or default persistence.

requirements.title: Larger balanced bank
requirements.acceptance: Target 80 distinct useful questions, release at least 60 across ten or more topics; ten starters then optional five-question blocks and explicit finish; no padding.

requirements.title: Correct semantic direction and fair scoring
requirements.acceptance: Every released mapping passes source-to-rubric calibration; visible answers are ordered -2 through +2; disclose comparable sets/unknowns and distinguish individual disagreement from aggregate overlap.

requirements.title: Modern readable accessible design
requirements.acceptance: One-question stage, equally readable choices, short smooth reduced-motion-safe transitions, clear selected/focus states and verified phone/keyboard/zoom/contrast behavior.

requirements.title: No optional collection dependency
requirements.acceptance: Feedback stays disabled and deferred; no quiz-data reuse or live collection. Preserve separate consent/privacy requirements for later.

requirements.title: Lean reused architecture
requirements.acceptance: One existing Laravel app, static excerpt-only bank and local source prep; no runtime model/new service/infrastructure/dependency expansion.

requirements.title: Explicit edition and corrections
requirements.acceptance: 2023 labels, exact programme locators, frozen sessions, small corrections/withdrawals/rollback and separate newly analysed future editions.

requirements.title: Evidence and commit discipline
requirements.acceptance: Actual acceptance evidence and required tests; exact staged CI before each main commit; no bypass/push/reset/history rewrite or revival of the old loop.

project.futureEditionPolicy: New programme reading and candidacy reconciliation produce a separate version; never relabel 2023 positions as current.

sourcePreparation.readings: Authored per-programme records keyed to original byte/text hashes and complete page ranges; no automatic summaries substituted for reading.

questionnaireDesign.selectionFormula: Retain the existing local selector only after real-bank coverage, family balance, burden and fairness checks. Selection may choose existing authored IDs; it must never create or rewrite a question.
questionnaireDesign.questionCountPolicy: Target 80 distinct useful questions; at least 60 evidence-supported released questions across 10 or more topics. Never pad with repetitions or invent positions to reach a quota. Report a quality shortfall and keep work open.
questionnaireDesign.cohortPolicy: Constituency defines eligible candidacies independently of answers. Rank only a disclosed fixed evidence-qualified subset on exactly the same answered propositions and weights; keep all other eligible candidacies visible with coverage and explicit limitations, never silently drop them. If no fair subset exists show unranked cited results.
questionnaireDesign.continuationPolicy: Ten balanced starter questions, deliberate finish or five more; continue in five-question blocks through 15/20/25/30 while useful unseen evidence exists. A larger authored bank is not a requirement to answer every question.

metricsDesign.iterationPolicy: No feedback expansion or live collection in this iteration. Preserve the separately voluntary protocol and security boundaries; future activation still requires actual hosted privacy/notice checks and explicit approval.

releaseContract.capabilityIsolation: Deferred comparison/metrics/translations do not block independently passing 2023 quiz.

policy.evidence: Actual commands/artifact hashes; local engineering does not certify production; preserve historical reports.

approvalGates.title: Concrete public action, costs and optional collection
approvalGates.scope: exact release/domain/provider/cost and explicitly included metric/statistic flags
approvalGates.requiredEvidence: Actual release checks, source provenance/permissions, authorized host flow/logs and restore/rollback; truthful metric notice/basis if enabled. No staff/quorum requirements.

phases.title: New acceptance baseline and reported defect
All real 2023 candidacies and source acquisition
Full reading, cross-reference and direct question authorship
Meaning, scoring, fair evidence and citations
Real release verification and reviewable public action
Deliberate deferrals and future edition preparation

audienceDesign.audience: A person who does not regularly follow politics or economics, using a phone, without prerequisite knowledge. Respectful adult language; no condescension.
questionContract: One concrete decision per question; one affirmative grammatical proposition whose positive answer always means agreeing with that exact proposition.
Spanish statement normally 12-25 words; if a longer statement is necessary preserve meaning and explain why. No unexplained acronym, double negation, two policies or leading moral label.
Optional neutral explanation, normally 25-45 words, describes what the proposal means; use everyday money/work/home/school/health/transport examples only when they preserve actual conditions.
Explain essential terms at first use (for example, the income tax on earnings); do not silently broaden a targeted tax into all taxes or a regional rule into all of Spain.
No unsupported impact forecast, guaranteed cheaper rent, inflation estimate or assertion that an opinion is correct. Plain-language examples are not proof of policy effects.
No party names, logos or ideological answer labels while answering. Original-language quotations and party identity become available in result evidence after deliberate finish.
No technical methodology/hashes/uncertainty tables in the main journey; retain source and method details behind clearly named optional disclosures.
resultContract: Start with a short Spanish explanation of the observed proposal overlap, not a voting instruction or a personality/ideology classification.

Show three understandable cited agreements and three disagreements when available, each with Your answer / What the programme proposes / How they relate. Do not fabricate six examples when evidence is absent.
Distinguish a disagreement on one proposal from total overlap across other proposals. A top overall result may disagree with the user on rent caps; label that disagreement explicitly.
Explain missing evidence as We could not find a clear position in this programme, never Neutral or They oppose it.
For fair ordering, explain These candidacies were compared using the same N questions; show other eligible candidacies and coverage. For insufficient evidence do not announce a winner.
Use a percentage only as a secondary explained policy-overlap index; no probability, confidence, sum-to-100 rule or definitive You are aligned with this party.
usefulnessAcceptance: Without opening methodology, the user can understand what decision each question asks about, choose unsure without penalty, edit an answer and explain why a shown result appeared.

Complete a reproducible phone/keyboard walkthrough of start, question help, answer, back/edit, checkpoint, finish, result difference, missing evidence and original citation. Fix any step requiring analyst knowledge.
Audit every released question and help text using this contract, with recorded revisions; a readability number or passing screenshot alone is not semantic validation.

visualDesign.direction: Quiz stage inspired by the clear one-question interaction of Kahoot, with a calm credible civic identity. No trivia right/wrong, speed score, countdown, competitive leaderboard or party-coloured answer buttons.
visualDesign.typography: Reuse the existing locally served font assets after inspecting them; strong readable sans headings, body 18px on mobile, line height 1.5-1.65, bounded line lengths; no third-party font request or dependency changes.
questionLayout: Compact persistent edition/progress line; topic name; one large question; optional What does this mean? help.
Five equally prominent labelled agreement choices in a stable disagree-to-agree order; separate unsure and skip controls. Native radio group, no hover-only controls.
Back/edit and one primary Continue action remain clear; selection has an immediate visible state, but no automatic advancement.
Checkpoint after ten: See my result or Five more questions; always explicit finish. Result page has plain-language agreement/difference evidence and a quiet source disclosure.

visualDesign.motion: Short 160-220ms opacity/transform transitions between questions and clear selected-state feedback; no layout jump, double submission or lost focus. prefers-reduced-motion removes movement and preserves feedback.
visualDesign.accessibility: 44px minimum touch targets, visible keyboard focus, radio keyboard semantics, text contrast at least 4.5:1, control/focus contrast at least 3:1; 320px reflow and 200/400% zoom; never encode direction only by colour. Verify the actual palette in each state.
visualDesign.performance: Reuse the fixed bank architecture and local fonts. Measure release payload and mobile interaction in the existing budget checks; animate transform/opacity and avoid blocking work per answer.
visualDesign.acceptance: Inspect actual desktop/mobile screenshots for intro/question/help/selected/checkpoint/results/loading/error states and perform keyboard/reduced-motion checks; no design task is complete from CSS or descriptions alone.
